# gawk-sampler test data

Nothing here is NudeNet: no weights, no code, no photograph (docs/71 §8.1,
§9.6). Each set is generated by the script beside it; regenerate rather than
edit.

| Directory | What | Generator |
|---|---|---|
| `models/` | `test-320.onnx`, `test-640.onnx`: NudeNet's input/output contract, scoring a frame's magenta share as `FEMALE_GENITALIA_EXPOSED`. CI and the dev stack load these instead of the real detector. | `models/generate.py` (needs `onnx`) |
| `reference/vectors/` | The real 320n model's candidate output rows on public-domain NASA photographs, and NudeNet's own detections from them. `TestDecodeMatchesNudeNetReference` holds the sampler's post-processing to them. Sources: `reference/SOURCES.md`. | `reference/generate.py` (needs `nudenet`, run against the photographs and the 320n weights) |
| `bitstreams/` | One keyframe per broadcaster codec — H.264 Annex B, VP8, VP9 — plus a solid-magenta H.264 frame. The tests build the web broadcaster's AVCC form from the Annex B one. | `bitstreams/generate.py` (needs an ffmpeg with libx264 and libvpx) |

The native tests find the real ffmpeg (`deploy/build-ffmpeg.sh`) and ONNX
Runtime through `GAWK_SAMPLER_FFMPEG` and `GAWK_SAMPLER_ONNXRUNTIME_LIB`, and
skip without them unless `GAWK_SAMPLER_REQUIRE_NATIVE=1`.
